articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Extended Reasoning and Native Multimodal Generation
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5, featuring significantly improved chain-of-thought reasoning, native image and audio generation, and a context window exceeding 1 million tokens. The model demonstrates substantial gains on graduate-level science and mathematics benchmarks, narrowing the gap with domain-specific expert systems. Enterprise API pricing reflects the increased compute cost but offers a distilled GPT-5-mini variant for latency-sensitive workloads.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Pro Tops Agentic Coding Benchmarks
articles.summary: DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Pro has set new state-of-the-art results on SWE-Bench Verified and HumanEval-Agent, demonstrating the ability to autonomously plan, write, test, and debug multi-file codebases. The model's integrated tool-use architecture allows it to invoke compilers, linters, and search within a single reasoning trace. The release intensifies competition with Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's Codex-successor offerings in the developer tooling market.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Begins: First Compliance Audits Target Foundation Model Providers
articles.summary: The European Union's AI Office has initiated its first formal compliance audits under the AI Act's general-purpose AI provisions, requesting detailed documentation from major foundation model providers operating in the EU. Companies must demonstrate adherence to transparency requirements, copyright compliance protocols, and systemic risk assessments. Legal analysts expect the outcomes to set important precedents for AI governance worldwide.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Demonstrates Autonomous Warehouse Operations at BMW Facility
articles.summary: Figure's second-generation humanoid robot, Figure 02, has completed a multi-week pilot at a BMW logistics facility in Spartanburg, SC, performing bin-picking, parts transport, and inventory scanning with minimal human oversight. The system leverages a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on manipulation tasks, achieving a reported 97% grasp success rate on previously unseen parts. BMW confirmed plans to expand the deployment to additional production lines by Q3 2026.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Toyota Research Institute Unveil Shared Dexterous Manipulation Platform
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics and TRI announced a joint open platform for dexterous robotic manipulation research, combining Atlas's hardware capabilities with TRI's diffusion-policy-based learning framework. The platform provides a standardized sim-to-real pipeline, dramatically reducing the time required to train contact-rich manipulation policies. The collaboration aims to accelerate the industry toward general-purpose robotic dexterity, with APIs and simulation environments being released under a permissive license.

articles.title: Microsoft and Quantinuum Demonstrate Fault-Tolerant Logical Qubit Operations Below Error Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Quantinuum reported achieving repeated rounds of fault-tolerant error correction on logical qubits with error rates below the threshold needed for scalable quantum computation. The demonstration used Quantinuum's trapped-ion H2 processor with Microsoft's qubit-virtualization layer, executing over 50 rounds of syndrome extraction without logical failure. Researchers say this milestone significantly de-risks the path to practically useful quantum algorithms within this decade.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Risk Production of 1.4nm Process Node Ahead of Schedule
articles.summary: TSMC announced that its A14 (1.4nm-class) process node has entered risk production at its Fab 20 complex in Hsinchu, roughly one quarter ahead of its original roadmap. The node uses gate-all-around nanosheet transistors and backside power delivery, offering a reported 15% speed improvement and 30% power reduction over N2. Major customers including Apple, Nvidia, and AMD are expected to tape out designs later this year for 2027 volume production.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces 'Constitutional Classifiers' to Defend Against Jailbreaks in Claude 4
articles.summary: Anthropic published a technical report detailing a new safety architecture called constitutional classifiers, integrated into the forthcoming Claude 4 model family. The system uses a lightweight auxiliary model trained via constitutional AI principles to classify and intercept adversarial prompt patterns in real time, reducing jailbreak success rates by over 95% on internal red-team benchmarks. The approach imposes less than 3% latency overhead, making it practical for production deployment at scale.
